title: Entity-definition schema + migration + per-tenant registry

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: Foundation: the entity definitions everything else generates from. No dependencies.

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; Second Brain hub 3ee5f890 (Cole Medin context-retriever pillar), 489d675d/29ecd697 (loopctl entity-relationship ideas). Agent-native: no web UI.
background.includes: loopctl's knowledge_search retrieves CURATED articles; there is no schema-driven, governed tool surface over STRUCTURED records. This story adds per-tenant entity definitions (the schema the tool generator + executor consume). Phase 1 backing source is loopctl's OWN structured tables (projects/stories/epics); tenant-supplied sources are explicitly out of scope (future).

story.as_a: a loopctl tenant admin (or an agent acting for one)
story.i_want_to: declare entity definitions — name, fields (name, type, filterable?, searchable?), relationships, and a backing source — persisted per tenant
story.so_that: the tool generator and executor can produce a governed, structured query surface from a single declaration instead of hand-written tools

rationale: Cole Medin's context-retriever frames an entity/schema layer as the production analogue of a Karpathy wiki's index: it tells the agent what it can query and how. That declaration must be a first-class, tenant-scoped, validated schema before any generation or execution — it is the allowlist that makes generated queries safe (US-30.3 can only expose fields an entity marks filterable/searchable).

acceptance_criteria.description: Ecto schema Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Entity (table entity_definitions): tenant_id, name (unique per tenant), backing_source (enum, phase 1: loopctl-internal sources only), fields (embedded/json list of %{name, type, filterable, searchable}), relationships (json), inserted_at/updated_at. tenant_id set programmatically, never cast.

Changeset validates: unique (tenant_id, name); every field has a known type; filterable/searchable are booleans; backing_source is one of the allowlisted phase-1 internal sources (reject arbitrary/tenant-supplied sources in v1); field names match a safe identifier pattern (no injection via field names).

Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Registry.for_tenant/1 returns a tenant's entity definitions (scope-enforced); get_entity/2 returns one by name within tenant. A definition from tenant A is invisible to tenant B.
Tenant isolation rides SetTenant/RLS on Loopctl.Repo for the definitions table; a two-tenant test proves A's entities are never returned in B's scope.
Down migration cleanly drops entity_definitions; migrations run green on a fresh DB.

test_cases.name: create + fetch an entity definition within tenant
steps: insert an Entity for a projects source with fields [%{name: "status", type: :string, filterable: true, searchable: false}]
expected_results: the entity is returned with its fields; unique-per-tenant enforced

test_cases.name: changeset rejects unsafe field name and unknown backing source
steps: build Entity changeset with a field name "status; DROP" and backing_source :tenant_supplied
expected_results: invalid: field-name pattern error + backing_source not-allowlisted error

test_cases.name: entity definitions are tenant-isolated
expected_results: tenant_b sees no entities; tenant_a sees its one

technical_notes: Backing sources v1: loopctl-internal only (projects via Loopctl.Projects, stories via Loopctl.WorkBreakdown.Story, epics). Tenant-supplied external sources are a future epic.
Field-name identifier validation is a security control (US-30.3 builds queries from these names) — restrict to ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$.
Tenant scoping via SetTenant/RLS on Loopctl.Repo (OLTP), same as other tenant-scoped schemas.
